title: Unbounded exchange invertibility under arbitrary coefficient restriction
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings in the coefficient universe and φ : R →+* S any ring map. For a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and K in D(X_et,S) [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the image under derived restriction of scalars of the S-coefficient canonical unbounded exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at K is invertible if and only if the R-coefficient exchange at the derived restriction of K is invertible. No properness, torsion, flatness, boundedness or exchange-invertibility assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D6J(3), coefficient restriction and canonical mate comparison

proof.text: Forgetting R- or S-module structure to abelian sheaves gives the same underlying complex before and after restriction along φ. Exactness identifies their derived underlying objects and inverse images. Apply the canonical unbounded abelian exchange comparison for each ring: after its invertible endpoint comparisons both forgotten exchanges equal the same abelian exchange. Hence their invertibility is equivalent.

Exact forgetting R-module structure commutes with homology and reflects isomorphisms sectionwise; its derived functor therefore reflects isomorphisms, so equivalence of the forgotten invertibility tests gives the asserted equivalence between the two R-derived morphisms.

proof_origin.place: Part (3) gives the direct-image comparisons; canonical exchange mate coherence is the additional assertion of lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison.
